items.excerpt: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not halt migrants President Donald Trump threatened on Thursday to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop more than a thousand migrants walking north toward the United States after last week's US election, ​warning that they would not be allowed to enter. Venezuela, Colombia to collaborate on border security following kidnappings The governments of Colombia and Venezuela said on Thursday they are willing to coordinate security efforts to combat transnational crime following two recent high-profile kidnappings along their 2,219-kilometer shared border. Colombia is seeking Venezuelan help locating the wife of a Colombian mayor and an army officer. Democrat Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat, becomes state's first Black senator since 1874 Democratic challenger Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi election for the US Senate, media projected on Wednesday, making him the Southern state's first Black senator since the Reconstruction era that followed the US Civil War. The result was a ‌stunning upset in the heavily Republican state and expanded on the national drubbing the Democrats delivered to President Donald Trump's Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections. It was also a historic victory for African Americans in a former slave state that was a hotbed of repression during the civil rights movement of the 1960s. Putin lets Europe join Ukraine peace talks, as Kyiv says Starshield disrupted again President Vladimir Putin agreed on Thursday to let European representatives join the next round of Ukraine peace talks, a US envoy said, though the Russian leader said Washington must work with its European allies to understand if they want peace or war in Ukraine. The move to give Europe a seat at the negotiating table at the next round of talks, which US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters after the talks, is a breakthrough. But Putin's comments underlined how difficult the negotiations could become, given sharp differences between Moscow and European capitals. Climate change made Indonesian fires more severe, ‌scientists say Wildfires that hit large parts of Indonesia from August to October and plunged much of Southeast Asia into hazardous smoke were made much worse by "record-breaking" heat caused by human-induced climate change, scientists said on Friday. While a very strong El Niño was the dominant factor in determining the extremely low levels of rainfall across Indonesia from July, human-induced climate change contributed around 1.6 degrees Celsius of additional heat during the fire season, said a ‌report by climate research group World Weather Attribution.

items.excerpt: #### Restrictions on me arbitrary, vague: Sonam Wangchuk Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday (November 12, 2026) described the restrictions imposed by the administration on him as “bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate” and conspicuously “not using words such as house arrest”. Invoking Section 163(1) of the BNSS, the Ladakh administration on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) evening shifted Mr. Wangchuk from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence. #### Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told The Hindu. Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project. ... #### Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. The company’s board said Mr. Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement. #### Washington DC shooting: One dead, four people injured Five people were shot on Thursday (November 12, 2026) in a trendy Washington, D.C., neighbourhood within walking distance of the White House, police said, and the suspected gunman shot himself as a swarm of officers responded to a nearby apartment building. One victim died in the shooting, said Jeffrey Carroll, interim chief with the Metropolitan Police Department. #### Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant’s suite of apps. Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether. #### Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu Yemen’s Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea. The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world’s largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation “targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone”, while a second “targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile”.

items.title: House Democratic leaders face fallout over untimely floor vote fumbles
items.excerpt: A week that was supposed to see House Democrats transition seamlessly from a landslide midterm victory to a leadership coronation has instead been pocked by surprise Republican victories on the House floor. Why it matters: Skeptics of Democratic leadership have seized on these strategic fumbles to cast doubt on their much-heralded managerial abilities in the lead-up to the party's leadership elections next week. - "It's really unfortunate that this happened this week when, obviously, that is a narrative we hear leadership portray," Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.) told Axios. - Rep.-elect Melat Kiros (D-Colo.) said this week has "certainly not given me confidence," and that the election was an "indictment on how our party has been operating thus far, and this is a big part of why." - "We do know that the Democratic caucus has blundered before on things, like whipping the votes to protect NPR last spring," said Rep.-elect Don Leonard (D-Ohio). "We botched that one." What happened: The House voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to quash an effort by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) to impeach Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, with support from all House Democrats present. - The outcome quickly sparked backlash because nearly a dozen House Democrats were absent, many of whom got caught in a traffic jam returning from an Elect Democratic Women event. - That was followed by an incident on Wednesday in which House Republicans passed a veterans bill by voice vote despite Democratic opposition. - The incidents follow a procedural blowup in September in which a pair of centrist House Democrats repeatedly broke with leadership and helped the GOP advance key bills. What they're saying: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), asked about these incidents by Axios, touted a different veterans bill Democrats forced to a successful floor vote on Thursday via a discharge petition. - "House Democrats once again successfully forced a vote on a piece of legislation designed to make life better for the American people," he said. - House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-Mass.) did not respond to Axios' question and walked off the House floor into her office. The intrigue: Even some current and incoming House Democrats who are voting for Jeffries as speaker acknowledged the vote was a black eye. - "I think everyone's frustrated with how that all went down, I'm not going to lie to you about that," said Rep.-elect Dan Koh (D-Mass.). - "People are pissed," a senior House Democrat told Axios. The other side: Other Democrats told Axios the absences were an inevitable reality of Congress, noting that several who missed votes have said they were attending to emergencies. - "I think everyone's explained what the situations were — somebody was recovering from surgery. There are certain things that are unavoidable," said Rep. Adelita Grijalva (D-Ariz.). - Others said the upshot is that House Democrats need to do a better job of getting to votes on time: "The general consensus among the new members is on Jan. 3, it's time to lock in," Rep.-elect Matt Little (D-Minn.) told Axios. Others said the speakership election offers a window into how Jeffries' approach to the speakership might play out over the coming year. - Jeffries has always taken a more hands-off approach than his predecessor, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.), preferring to let issues and fights among members resolve themselves.

items.title: Democrats seek bipartisan path to immigration reform - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
items.excerpt: ## Democrats seek bipartisan path to immigration reform Anwar Iqbal Published November 13, 2026 Updated November 13, 2026 06:58am • Call for legal status for long-settled immigrants; plan congressional scrutiny of Homeland Security • Democratic states move to curb local agencies’ role in federal immigration efforts WASHINGTON: Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday called for a bipartisan immigration deal, seeking changes to President Donald Trump’s enforcement policies and legal status for long-settled immigrants. The appeal came as Democratic officials in several states and cities moved to limit their agencies’ role in federal immigration operations. Members of the House and Senate, including lawmakers elected last week, held a news conference outside the US Capitol. The group said election results offered an opportunity to revisit an approach deemed politically costly for Republicans. Representative Veronica Escobar, whose Texas district includes the border city of El Paso, said she wanted far-reaching reform but recognised legislation cannot pass without Republican support. “As we continue to have Donald Trump in the White House, and without a supermajority in the Senate, we need Republican support,” she said, adding that comprehensive reform would therefore have to be bipartisan. Senator Ruben Gallego of Arizona urged both parties to pursue an agreement before the congressional session ends, or continue negotiations in the next. Republicans long made immigration reform conditional on securing the border. “We have that right now. We did the job,” Gallego said. “Now let’s figure out how to right-size our immigration issue. Let’s figure out how to keep families together.” Representative Sylvia Garcia of Texas proposed starting with the Dream and Promise Act to provide a basis for broader changes when Democrats take control of Congress in January. Concurrently, state and local Democratic administrations moved to limit the role of their police and detention agencies in enforcing federal civil immigration rules. Houston Mayor John Whitmire issued an order barring police from contacting US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) regarding administrative immigration warrants during routine traffic stops and minor, nonviolent violations. Police may still contact ICE when a person booked into jail for a new offence carrying possible jail time also has an administrative warrant. The order removes provisions requiring officers to wait for extended periods for ICE agents to attend traffic stops or detention scenes. Whitmire consulted Texas’s newly elected governor, lieutenant governor and comptroller before acting, describing the move as an att­empt to ease immigrant communities’ anxiety. Whitmire opposed a 2017 Texas law prohibiting sanctuary-city policies when he was a state senator. The move follows major Democratic statewide gains: Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, and James Talarico won a Senate seat. Abbott earlier threatened to withhold over $110 million in safety grants from Houston over its limits on ICE cooperation. Austin and San Antonio are also reviewing their federal arrangements. Similar changes are occurring elsewhere. Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger ordered state law enforcement agencies to end 287(g) agreements with ICE, which authorise participating local officers to carry out specified immigration duties. Maryland Governor Wes Moore signed legislation ending formal 287(g) partnerships between ICE and local agencies. In New York, a law signed by Governor Kathy Hochul requires local detention facilities’ arrangements with federal immigration detention to end by Nov 25 . California continues applying its Values Act, restricting police resources for federal immigration enforcement. In January, Democrats plan to use congressional committee leadership to scrutinise the Department of Homeland Security, investigate enforcement practices and seek records. However, a majority alone cannot undo the president’s policies. Trump can veto legislation, and Senate rules make passing major measures difficult without broader support.

items.title: Celeb roundup: John Legend's SA tour, Kaytranada's return and more entertainment news
items.excerpt: 13 NOV 2026, 05:00 ... ## 1. John Legend announces three-city South African tour 13-time Grammy Award winner John Legend is scheduled to bring his The Muse Tour to the country in February 2027. The American singer-songwriter will perform in Pretoria on February 20 at SunBet Arena, before heading to the Durban ICC on February 23. His final South African show will take place at Cape Town’s Grand Arena, GrandWest, on February 25. Fans can expect to hear some of his best-known songs, including “All of Me”, “Ordinary People” and “Tonight (Best You Ever Had)”. Mastercard cardholders will have access to a presale beginning on November 11 at 10am, closing on November 13 at 8.59am. Eligible World, World Elite and World Legend cardholders will also have access to selected tickets from November 13 at 9am. ## 2. Yung Miami joins Ndlala Grandeur concert line-up Yung Miami joins the line-up for Ndlala Grandeur’s debut season. ... American rapper Yung Miami has been added to the international line-up for Ndlala Grandeur Season 1, with her performance scheduled for December 19. The luxury R&B concert series will run across five nights, from December 16 to 20, 2026. Other announced performers include Tamar Braxton, Eric Benét, DVSN, Chante Moore, Jac Ross and actor Ricco Ross, who will host the event. Nicole Murphy is also among the names announced. The extended concert series is set to bring together international R&B performers across the five-day event. ## 3. Kaytranada returns for Milk + Cookies Music Week Kaytranada will headline Milk + Cookies Music Week events in Cape Town and Johannesburg. Picture: File Grammy-winning producer and DJ Kaytranada is returning to South Africa in December, with performances planned for Cape Town on December 18 and Johannesburg on December 20. The shows will launch Milk + Cookies Music Week ahead of the festival’s third edition in January 2027. Rapper Lou Phelps will join him in both cities, alongside local performers. The Cape Town line-up includes Jinji, Kid Fonque, Kudbeu, Mamthug and Tumi Moliko, while MCHLSN, Muzi, Shamiso, Thakzin and Yolophonik are set to perform in Johannesburg. Kaytranada previously headlined the festival’s South African debut in 2025, where he reportedly performed for an audience of 20,000. The upcoming programme will extend beyond music, with organisers planning fashion and merchandise collaborations, yacht parties, industry discussions, writing workshops and community initiatives. ## 4. Sipho Chaine marries actress Kay Bikitsha ... Orlando Pirates goalkeeper Sipho Chaine and actress Kamvelihle “Kay” Bikitsha have confirmed that they are married. The couple shared the news in a joint Instagram post on Sunday, November 8, alongside photographs from their celebrations. Their announcement was accompanied by the caption, “Mr and Mrs Chaine… Thank you, Jesus.” ... ## 6. Inkabi Records responds to allegations surrounding Lwah Ndlunkulu ... Inkabi Records has rejected claims that the label is responsible for singer Lwah Ndlunkulu’s health difficulties, following growing public discussion about her wellbeing and professional relationship with the company. In a statement, the label said its engagement with the singer and her family pointed to personal circumstances, including substance-use concerns, as the source of her current challenges. It also said doctors had assessed her for psychosis, and that it had worked with her family to arrange professional help at a wellness facility, with the label covering the costs. The label also defended its contractual and financial arrangements with the singer, saying her grandfather, Dr Sipho Sithole, was familiar with the agreements from early in her career. It asked the public to respect her privacy. ## 7. Tony Forbes seeks musicians to help complete song dedicated to AKA ... Tony Forbes has opened up about his ongoing grief over the death of his son, Kiernan “AKA” Forbes, while appealing to singers and rappers to help him finish a song they had once planned to create together. In an Instagram post, Forbes reflected on the time that has passed since his son’s death, admitting that although he often ... He said he has been finding a renewed sense of purpose through projects that have helped him with the healing process. One of those projects is a song he began working on more than a year ago. Forbes explained that he had previously persuaded AKA to collaborate with him, but they ran out of time before they could complete it. He decided to continue with the idea, writing lyrics and recording an early demo with help from Al. The project later progressed to a rough recording with another artist, but that collaboration came to a halt when the vocalist became unavailable. Forbes is now inviting singers and rappers who are interested in helping him bring the song to life to contact him directly, preferably with a vocal sample. ## 8. Kylie Jenner faces another lawsuit from former housekeeper ... Reality television star Kylie Jenner and members of her team are facing another lawsuit from a former housekeeper who alleges she experienced mistreatment while working for the star. The lawsuit, filed by Dinora Carolina Cabria Amaya in California, includes claims that she was kept inside Jenner’s closet for more than an hour, bitten by a dog while carrying out cleaning duties and exposed to pepper spray that allegedly discharged into her face and eyes. Amaya also claims she was wrongfully dismissed in February after raising concerns about her wages and treatment at work. She said she was paid $40 (around R660) an hour from March 2025 and alleges that her duties included setting up a massage table for Jenner and carrying heavy rubbish bags. She is seeking compensation for lost earnings and employment benefits, as well as emotional distress and other damages. No specific amount has been stated. The filing is reportedly the fourth lawsuit brought against Jenner and members of her team since April 2026.
